newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African long bonds recouped intraday losses to end unchanged from their closing levels on Friday after an initial spike higher in yields in early trade.
The rand was also little changed from its previous close as activity was hampered by holidays in New York and London.
At 1410 GMT the R150 was unchanged from late Friday at a 15.04 percent yield after bouncing off 15.11 percent in the morning -- its worst level in a month.
Bond traders noted that the bond market had weakened close to 30 basis points from the start of last week.
"It's a combination of a poor technical outlook, a weaker rand and caution ahead of the money supply and private sector credit figures on Wednesday," one senior trader said.
Another said buying had simply dried up.
"We saw some good demand for stock in the past but now there is a lack of buyers," he noted, attributing this in part to caution ahead of the release of key economic figures.
Players were loathe to go long ahead of the M3 and credit figures on Wednesday at 1500 GMT and the bigger institutions were waiting for the data for fresh signals whether to buy or sell, he said.
Other numbers due this week are April trade figures due out on Tuesday at 1200 GMT, inflation at 0900 GMT on Wednesday and first quarter GDP on Thursday at 0730 GMT.
Dealers expected the market to be range-bound on Tuesday ahead of the M3 data, with 15.11 percent seen toppish.
A Reuters concensus poll of eight economists forecast a 900 million rand trade surplus from a 1.98 billion rand surplus in March.

In a separate poll, eleven economists forecast both April money supply and credit to climb, calling for a 16.70 percent year-on-year rise in money supply growth from a preliminary 16.39 percent increase in March.
Growth in credit extension was seen rising 16.40 percent from 15.96 percent previously.
Foreigners were net sellers of 338.10 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Friday after selling 821.54 million rand's worth on Thursday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal turnover on the exchange was 5.52 billion rand on Friday after soaring to 39.84 billion rand on Thursday -- a settlement date.
Trade on the forex side was generally muted and the rand managed to hold below the 4.48 level but traders said a break above there was possible as the week progressed.
"One specific local bank bought dollar throughout the day, knocking the rand but there were also a few export orders," a senior trader said.
He said the Reserve Bank continued to show a presence in the market, wanting to prevent a move above the 4.48 level.

Another trader at a leading bank said 4.4980 was the crucial level to watch. Any move above that level would trigger stop loss dollar buying, particularly from some London investment houses which were sitting short in dollars.
Tuesday's range was seen between 4.46 to 4.49 and activity was expected to liven up as New York and London traders returned from Monday's holiday.
In cross rate action, the rand was last at 0.3775/3779 to the mark -- which was higher in Europe against the franc and lira following French elections on Sunday -- from 0.3780/3784 marks on Friday.
The local unit was changing hands at 26.0170/0456 yen from 25.7951/8236 yen previously and 7.3293/3387 rand to the British pound from 7.2859/2934 before.
South Africa's money market shortage rose to 6.700 billion rand on Saturday from 6.313 billion on Friday, the Reserve Bank said
Three-month NCD rates remained unchanged from Friday at 16.35 percent offered, as did 90-day BA rates which lined up at 15.85 percent.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482-1003
